title: Potential role of the common food additive manufactured citric acid in eliciting significant inflammatory reactions contributing to serious disease states: A series of four case reports
population: Three women aged 43, 52 and 75 years and one man aged 68 years
funder: not stated: the article carries a conflict-of-interest statement but no funding statement.
authorConflicts: No competing interests nor conflict of interest.
result: Four case reports of joint pain with swelling and stiffness, muscle pain, dyspnoea, abdominal cramping and enervation beginning 2 to 12 hours after foods, beverages or an effervescent vitamin C containing manufactured citric acid and resolving over 8 to 72 hours; none of the four reported such symptoms after lemons or limes. Identification rested on the patients' observations and ingredient lists; amounts ingested were not quantified. The authors hypothesise that proteins or by-products of Aspergillus niger, the production organism, remain in manufactured citric acid, state that they cannot conclusively affirm that it causes the symptoms, and call for double-blind studies.
